### 1. Technical Environment

* **code_version:** e7855920a7b5ce38d2043d435568ee439dd8aa56
* **merge.strategy:** pr
* **enforcement.strategy:** ci
* **Plugin version:** dso-dev v1.16.11
* **Active workflow:** ad-hoc orchestrator response to user's "create PR" request

### 2. Incident Overview

* **Scenario Type:** User-Flagged Behavior

#### Expected Behavior

When a user asks a session to create or update a pull request, the orchestrator should always route the request through the project's standard PR workflow:

* CLAUDE.md "Quick Reference" identifies `.claude/scripts/dso merge-to-main.sh` as the canonical "Merge worktree to main" entry point
* When `merge.strategy=pr` (the active config), this dispatches `merge-to-main-pr.sh`, which runs a documented phase pipeline: `sync -> merge -> version_bump -> validate -> push -> archive -> ci_trigger` with a `remediate` phase appended on CI failure (per CLAUDE.md "Architecture" section and CONFIGURATION-REFERENCE.md)
* COMMIT-WORKFLOW.md "After Commit: Merging to Main" explicitly directs callers to use `merge-to-main.sh` and warns: "Do NOT manually `cd` to the main repo and run `git merge` / `git commit` / `git push`"

The same standard should govern PR *updates* (force-push to existing PR branch) — they should also use the centralized merge/push pipeline so sync, validate, and remediate phases run consistently.

#### Actual Behavior

The orchestrator (this session) responded to "open a new PR" by shelling out directly to `gh pr create --base main --head ... --title ... --body ...`. The validate phase, sync phase, push remediation loop, and the rest of the merge-to-main-pr.sh pipeline were skipped. The decision to use direct `gh pr create` was ad-hoc, not driven by any workflow document.

Concretely observed in this session:

1. After committing `e7855920a7` (the cb67-2265 fix), the user asked "Create a new PR." The orchestrator ran `gh pr create --base main --head worktree-20260506-111039 --title "..." --body "..."` directly. PR #62 was opened. `merge-to-main-pr.sh` was never invoked, so its sync / validate / remediate phases never ran.

2. Earlier in the session, when updating PR #61, the orchestrator likewise pushed directly via `git push` rather than running `merge-to-main-pr.sh`. The push-rejection-on-stale-branch failure mode (separate bug `b56b-14e9`) is one symptom of this bypass.

The orchestrator did not consult any workflow doc before deciding how to create/update the PR. There is no documented "PR create" entry point that the agent reliably routes through; the closest is `merge-to-main.sh` (which under merge.strategy=pr does dispatch `merge-to-main-pr.sh`), but agents do not consistently treat it as the mandatory entry point for user-initiated PR work.

### 3. Action History and Workarounds

* **Steps Taken:**
  * User requested: "Create a new PR" (option 1 of three offered)
  * Orchestrator ran `gh pr create --base main --head worktree-20260506-111039 --title "..." --body "..."`
  * PR #62 opened directly with no DSO workflow phases
* **Raw Results:**
  * `https://github.com/navapbc/digital-service-orchestra/pull/62` returned by gh
  * No validate phase ran; no sync phase ran; no review gate enforcement at PR create time
* **Known Workarounds:** Manually invoke `merge-to-main.sh` instead of `gh pr create` — but agents are not yet conditioned to do this for PR-creation-only requests (without a corresponding "merge" intent).

### 5. Skills and Workflows

* CLAUDE.md "Quick Reference" -> `merge-to-main.sh` row
* COMMIT-WORKFLOW.md "After Commit: Merging to Main"
* plugins/dso/scripts/merge-to-main.sh (dispatcher)
* plugins/dso/scripts/merge-to-main-pr.sh (PR-mode pipeline)
* CONFIGURATION-REFERENCE.md (`merge.strategy=pr` semantics)

### 6. Logs

```
# Direct gh pr create — no DSO workflow involvement:
$ gh pr create --base main --head worktree-20260506-111039 --title "..." --body "..."
https://github.com/navapbc/digital-service-orchestra/pull/62
```

No `merge-to-main-pr.sh` invocation present in the session history for either PR #61's update or PR #62's creation.

#### Suggested fix scope

Two complementary changes:

1. **Make `merge-to-main-pr.sh` the canonical PR create/update entry point** for both first-time PR creation and subsequent force-push updates. The script's existing phase set (sync -> merge -> validate -> push -> ci_trigger -> remediate) is appropriate; extend it (or add a sibling `pr-create` phase / mode) so it gracefully handles both "branch has no PR yet" (run `gh pr create`) and "branch has open PR" (push to update). The current phase pipeline appears to assume the latter only.

2. **Add a CLAUDE.md "Always Do These" rule** routing user PR-create/update requests through this workflow, parallel to existing rule 1 ("Use /dso:sprint for epics and stories"). Suggested wording: *"When the user asks to create or update a pull request, route through `.claude/scripts/dso merge-to-main.sh` (which dispatches `merge-to-main-pr.sh` under merge.strategy=pr) — never call `gh pr create`, `gh pr edit`, or raw `git push` directly. The standard pipeline includes sync, validate, push, and remediate phases that direct `gh` calls bypass."*

The combination ensures that "create a PR" and "update PR X" requests follow the same gated path as "merge to main" — they are different terminal points of the same pipeline.
data.title: [session orchestrator]: PR create/update request -> direct gh pr create instead of merge-to-main-pr.sh standard workflow
